correctness.rationale: Inclusion--exclusion gives the exact covariance entries and their strict off-diagonal signs. For at least two draws, positive-probability singleton and pair occupancy patterns force every zero-variance linear combination to be zero, proving positive definiteness. Diagonal normalization then writes the matrix as I-B with B nonnegative and spectral radius below one; the Neumann series proves every inverse entry strictly positive. Exact-rational sample-space enumeration and inversion replay the formulas on finite instances.

value.rationale: Occupied- and empty-category indicators are standard objects in species sampling, coupon collection, categorical data, and balls-and-bins models. The covariance inverse governs linear conditioning and generalized least-squares geometry, so its strict sign pattern is substantially stronger than pairwise negative covariance. The exact transition from rank m-1 at one draw to positive definiteness at two draws is a natural structural classification.
